circuit_934 - a single-loop-plus-shunts network. A 4u(-t)V source on the left column (x~185) drives a series 3ohm + 0.25H along the top rail (y~370-385); the rail then feeds three parallel shunt branches to the bottom rail (y~618): a 0.1F capacitor at x~504, a 5ohm resistor at x~645, and a 4u(t)A current source at x~770. The GND symbol hangs below the bottom rail at x~499, so the whole bottom rail is net 0.

NET MAP (4 nets, 7 components):
  n3 = top-left: V-DC top/+ terminal (188,449) -> up x=186 -> top rail corner -> left lead of the 3ohm resistor (220,367).
  n1 = short top-rail segment between the 3ohm and the 0.25H, x ~330..351: resistor#1 right lead and inductor#0 left lead.
  n2 = the whole top rail right of the inductor, x ~464..775 (y 384->390): inductor#0 right lead (464,384), capacitor#4 top plate (504,463) via site S6, 5ohm resistor#2 top (649,417) via site S7, and the current source#3 top (775,454) at the top-right corner.
  0  = the bottom rail y~615..625 from x=185 to x=770, plus the GND stub down to (497,647): V-DC bottom (181,533), capacitor#4 bottom (505,531), 5ohm bottom (648,528) via site S14, current source#3 bottom (771,552), GND#6.

CRITICAL SITE DECISIONS (all four read as JUNCTION):
  S6 (505,387) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the top rail runs left-to-right and the capacitor column drops away below it. There is a small ink thickening just right of the meeting point but no hop and no pass-through geometry. A non-join would strand the capacitor's top plate on a one-terminal net.
  S7 (647,388) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the 5ohm resistor's top lead ends on the top rail. Same argument.
  S14 (643,621) deg=3 -> JUNCTION. Plain T: the 5ohm resistor's bottom lead ends on the bottom rail, with a slight blob at the contact. Same argument.
  S16 (500,625) deg=4 dot=2.1 -> JUNCTION. The only 4-way on the sheet: the capacitor column comes down from above, the bottom rail passes through horizontally, and the GND stub continues below. The crop shows a plain cross with a modest thickening and NO semicircular hop or sideways jog. Reading it as a CROSSING would put {capacitor bottom, GND} on one net and {V-DC bottom, 5ohm bottom, current source bottom} on another - the source loop would then have no ground reference at all and, more decisively, the 4u(-t)V source's return would never reach the capacitor branch that the top rail feeds, leaving the capacitor in a dead-end series path with only the ground symbol. Electrical impossibility settles it: junction.

PORT FIXES (three terminals had landed on handwritten label ink, each producing a one-terminal net):
  #1 Resistor (3ohm) t1: was port p2 @(318,339), a stroke of the '3R' label written above the zigzag. Moved to p4 @(330,377), the real right-hand lead - the same wire run (wire_len 22) that the inductor's left lead sits on, so this merged the old singletons n4 and n1.
  #3 I-DC (4u(t)A) t0: was port p2 @(716,494), which is the tail of the omega in the '5R' label written to the right of the 5ohm resistor - it happens to reach the current source's bounding box. Moved to p1 @(771,552), the real bottom lead, which joins the bottom rail (net 0). Removed spurious net n5. (Terminal order is unscored for a 2-terminal source, so t0=bottom / t1=top is fine.)
  #5 V-DC (4u(-t)V) t0: was port p3 @(138,504), a stroke of the '4u(-t)V' label to the left of the circle. Moved to p0 @(181,533), the real bottom lead, which joins the bottom rail (net 0). Removed spurious net n6.
After these three fixes every net has at least two terminals.

Other checks: #2 Resistor p1 @(671,498) and p3 @(671,473) are the '5R' label and were correctly not used; #0 Inductor p1 @(440,345) is the '0.25H' label and was correctly not used. All classes match the drawn symbols (circle with +/- bars = V-DC, circle with a plain up-arrow = I-DC, the curved-plate symbol at x~504 = Capacitor). No 3-terminal parts, so no pin-order questions. Non-critical sites S2, S3, S4, S8, S9, S11, S12 are all handwritten-label ink ('3R', '0.25H', '5R', '4u(-t)V') brushing a wire or a component box and change nothing. Nothing unresolved.
